name: Vespid Dynamics Swarm Relay Beacon SRB-4
product_name: Vespid Dynamics Swarm Relay Beacon SRB-4
description: A portable beacon that serves as a command-and-control relay point for Vespid drone swarms, extending operational range and providing a rally point for autonomous drone assets. The SRB-4 broadcasts encrypted control signals, collects sensor data from drones within range, and can serve as an autonomous command node if communication with the primary controller is lost. Multiple beacons can be networked to create a mesh of relay points covering an entire operational area. The beacon also serves as a charging station for micro-drones, with inductive pads that recharge up to four drones simultaneously.

specifications.autonomous mode: Maintains last orders if controller lost

story_hooks: SRB-4 beacons have been found placed throughout a Tier 2 district in a grid pattern — someone is building a drone operations infrastructure across the entire district without authorization.

An SRB-4 in autonomous mode has been maintaining a drone patrol pattern around a building for three weeks after its controller was killed — the drones are protecting something their dead operator cared about.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek cylindrical command beacon resembling a tactical flashlight crossed with a communications relay. The form is purposefully compact and mobile, designed for rapid deployment across urban and industrial environments. Its tapered top narrows to a broadcasting antenna array, while the base widens slightly to accommodate inductive charging pads and a heavy-duty magnetic mounting system.
physical_description.dimensions: 15 cm tall, approximately 5 cm diameter at widest point (base)
physical_description.weight_description: 0.8 kg—handheld and pocketable in tactical gear, though typically carried in a quick-access pouch or mounted via magnetic base
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer composite housing with embedded copper mesh shielding; aluminum alloy base ring
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal with subtle anti-reflective coating; visible heatsink ribbing along upper cylinder; polished aluminum charging contacts
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte charcoal gray body with electric teal accent strips running vertically; bronze/copper inductive charging pad rings visible at base; faint phosphorescent emergency stripe
physical_description.interface_elements: Top-mounted status LED ring (multicolor: green for active relay, amber for mesh connection, red for low power); four flush inductive charging pads arranged in circular pattern on base; recessed toggle power switch; small diagnostic holodisplay port (3mm); integrated antenna array at apex with micro-adjustable pivot joints
distinctive_features: Layered antenna crown with 6 articulated micro-relay spines that physically fan out when powered
Four inductive charging pads that glow faintly blue during active charging cycle
Mesh networking indicator: secondary LED band that pulses to show connected beacon count in local network
Magnetic base with adjustable tension—strong enough to hold on moving vehicles or drones
Vespid security hologram on lower cylinder that shifts color when tilted (anti-counterfeit measure)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Vespid Dynamics logo embossed on upper third; 'SRB-4' designation below logo; regulatory stamps (GLMZ compliance, QUANTA pricing: Φ2,400); serial number laser-etched on base ring
physical_description.condition_typical: In field deployment, typically mounted magnetically on vehicle dash, rooftop relay point, or held by handler in tactical harness. Charging pads show minor scuff marks from micro-drone contacts. Antenna spines are often slightly oriented toward signal source.
